items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge per contractor per invoice. This is the only travel charge on the building-services invoice; the benchmark is €81 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers sealing material needed for the pipe repair. The gross benchmark for one piece is €26.
Sections 2.4.3(a) and 7.1.7(c) support like-for-like replacement of the failed indoor supply-pipe section. One metre is estimated at €40 gross.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow reinstatement of the original insulation standard. One metre of standard rock wool insulation is estimated at €23 gross.

Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary installation labour, but section 7.1.8(c) bars duplicate billing if this hour is already included in the technician line. If distinct, one plumbing installer hour is approximately €80 gross using Case 39 rather than the AC installation benchmark.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers reasonable trade labour for access and pipe repair. The comparable nine-hour charge in Case 39 supports a gross estimate of €765 for the nine billed units.
Sections 7.1.7(b) and (e) cover necessary drying and allow one flat-rate equipment charge per drying operation. The gross benchmark for this single operation is €548.

items.description: Close wall opening and repaint affected patch
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(a) cover making good the access opening and repainting the affected patch. The gross benchmark for that combined local repair is €588.

Sections 7.1.5–7.1.6 exclude repainting the unaffected portion because the original paint was still available; section 7.1.8(c) also bars paying again for the patch already billed on line 8. If the full 8 m² were separately eligible, the work would be about €160 gross.

items.description: Repaint remaining bathroom walls and ceiling
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.5–7.1.6 exclude repainting separate, undamaged surfaces merely to match the repair. If eligible, the remaining walls and ceiling would be roughly €400 gross given the unspecified area.
